result.topic_en: Riemann discusses when the heat equation admits solutions depending on a single variable α (isothermal surfaces), reducing the problem to finding functions α of x,y,z with Δα=0 and |∇α|² = f(α), and begins treating the case where p,q,r are independent via a Legendre transformation.
result.transcription:
$\alpha$ pendebit, in duas discinditur:
$a'\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}+b'\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ $\quad a''\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}+b''\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}=0$
Quarum secunda introducta nova variabili loco
$\alpha$ transformatur in $\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha^2}=0$, unde $u$ formam induet:
$u_1\alpha+u_2$ denotantibus $u_1u_2$ functiones temporis.
Hinc prima aequationum, modo posteriorum
formam induet:
$(c\alpha+c_1)\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
denotantibus $c, c_1$ constantes, unde:
$cu_1=\frac{\partial u_1}{\partial t}$ $\quad 0=\frac{\partial u_2}{\partial t}$
et $u$ erit formae $\alpha e^{ct}+$ const.
In casu secundo, si in aequatione 1. a et b
sola variabili $\alpha$ pendent, semper supponere licet
$b=0$, et quum aequatio 1. sit transformata hujus:
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial z^2}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
Quaestio in hanc revocata est:
Invenire omnes functiones $\alpha$ coordinatarum $x,y,z$,
duabus aequationibus satisfacientes;
1. $\Delta\varphi=\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial y^2}+\frac{\partial^2\alpha}{\partial z^2}=0$ ; $D=(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x})^2+(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial y})^2+(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial z})^2=f(\alpha)$
Ponamus brevitatis causa:
$\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x}=p$ , $\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial y}=q$ , $\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial z}=r$ ; $p^2+q^2+r^2=m$
et distinguamus [-duo-] {+quatuor+} casus:
1° Si $p,q,r$ sunt functiones independentes coordinatarum $x,y,z$ erit $\alpha$ functio ipsius $m$ [-a-] quam per
$\varphi(m)$ designamus. Deinde $p,q,r$ tanquam variabiles
independentes introducimus; ponendo:
$s=\alpha-xp-yq-zr$ ; $ds=-x\,dp-y\,dq-z\,dr$
unde:
$x=-\frac{\partial s}{\partial p}$ , $y=-\frac{\partial s}{\partial q}$ , $z=-\frac{\partial s}{\partial r}$
$s-p\frac{\partial s}{\partial p}-q\frac{\partial s}{\partial q}-r\frac{\partial s}{\partial r}=\alpha=\varphi(m)$
et posito:
$s=\psi(m)+t$ $\quad \psi(m)-2m\psi'(m)=\varphi(m)$ ;
$t-p\frac{\partial t}{\partial p}-q\frac{\partial t}{\partial q}-r\frac{\partial t}{\partial r}=0$
Cujus aequationis solutio generalis est:
$t=p\,\chi(\frac{q}{p},\frac{r}{p})=p\,\chi(\beta,\gamma)$
denotante $\chi$ functionem arbitrariam, et $\beta=\frac{q}{p}$, $\gamma=\frac{r}{p}$
unde:
$-x=\frac{\partial s}{\partial p}=2p\psi'(m)+\chi-\beta\chi'(\beta)-\gamma\chi'(\gamma)$
2. $\quad -y=\frac{\partial s}{\partial q}=2q\psi'(m)+\chi'(\beta)$
$-z=\frac{\partial s}{\partial r}=2r\psi'(m)+\chi'(\gamma)$
Porro ex aequatione
$\Delta=\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial r}{\partial z}=0$
